Data source overview:
The text is a mathematical note that derives necessary and sufficient conditions for a twice-differentiable objective function to be strongly convex with respect to arbitrary norms. It works through special cases (ℓ2, ℓ∞, ℓ1) and ends with a general theorem stating that strong convexity is equivalent to the Hessian dominating a finite set of rank-one positive-semidefinite matrices determined by the dual norm geometry.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83]

Inference strategy justification:
The document is purely theoretical and does not explicitly discuss practical AI safety interventions. Moderate inference (confidence ≤ 2) was therefore applied to map its mathematical results to plausible AI-safety-relevant actions: (i) auditing objective functions for strong convexity during model design and (ii) adding appropriate regularisation terms to enforce the derived Hessian lower-bounds. All other edges rely on explicit logical steps or formally proven theorems in the text (confidence ≥ 4).

Extraction completeness explanation:
All distinct claims that participate in causal reasoning—from the risk of convergence instability, through mechanisms (absence of strong convexity), through the hierarchy of formal criteria, to actionable design-time interventions—have been included and interconnected. Every node is referenced by at least one edge, and no edge links a risk node directly to an intervention node. Framework decomposition is not applicable because the text does not introduce a monolithic framework.

Key limitations:
1. The risk of “convergence instability” is not explicitly stated in the source; it is inferred from standard optimisation theory.
2. Implementation details of the inferred interventions are schematic because the paper is theoretical.
3. Section titles are absent in the source; paragraph identifiers were approximated for traceability.

Instruction-set improvement:
Allow citing paragraph numbers when section titles are missing, and clarify how to handle purely theoretical papers whose practical interventions must be inferred.
